Mapping ER to relational schema transforms entities into tables and relationships into foreign keys
Foreign key is an attribute that references primary key of another table
Primary key uniquely identifies each row in a table
student_answer: Primary key is unique and not null

model_answer: Candidate key is a minimal superkey that uniquely identifies rows
student_answer: Candidate keys are potential primary keys

model_answer: Superkey is any set of attributes that uniquely identifies a row
Referential integrity ensures foreign key values match primary key values or are null
Check constraint limits values in a column
Unique constraint ensures all values in a column are distinct
Default constraint assigns a default value when none provided
Composite key is a primary key consisting of two or more attributes
A surrogate key is an artificial primary key
student_answer: Auto-increment ID is a surrogate key

model_answer: Normalization removes redundancy and improves data integrity
First normal form (1NF) eliminates repeating groups
Second normal form (2NF) removes partial dependencies
student_answer: Partial dependency on composite key removed in 2NF

model_answer: Third normal form (3NF) removes transitive dependencies
student_answer: Non-key should not depend on another non-key

model_answer: BCNF is stricter than 3NF; every determinant must be a candidate key
Denormalization adds redundancy to improve query performance
Functional dependency means one attribute determines another
student_answer: A -> B means A determines B

model_answer: Lossless join decomposition ensures no spurious tuples
Dependency preservation means all FDs are enforced without joins
student_answer: Each FD is checked in one table

model_answer: Closure of attributes is all attributes functionally determined by a set
SELECT statement retrieves data from a database
WHERE clause filters rows based on conditions
JOIN combines rows from two or more tables
GROUP BY groups rows that have the same values
HAVING filters groups after GROUP BY
ORDER BY sorts result set
INSERT adds new rows to a table
UPDATE modifies existing rows
student_answer: UPDATE employees SET salary = 60000 WHERE id = 1

model_answer: DELETE removes rows from a table
CREATE TABLE defines a new table
student_answer: CREATE TABLE users (id INT, name VARCHAR)

model_answer: ALTER TABLE modifies an existing table
student_answer: ALTER TABLE users ADD email VARCHAR

model_answer: DROP TABLE deletes a table
Subquery is a query inside another query
student_answer: SELECT name FROM users WHERE id IN (SELECT user_id FROM orders)

model_answer: EXISTS checks for existence of rows in a subquery
Aggregate functions: COUNT, SUM, AVG, MIN, MAX
DISTINCT eliminates duplicate rows
Stored procedure is precompiled SQL code stored on the server
Function returns a single value and can be used in expressions
Trigger executes automatically on DML events
student_answer: Trigger runs before or after INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE

model_answer: Cursor allows row-by-row processing of query results
student_answer: Used when set operations are insufficient

Exception handling in SQL catches runtime errors

Savepoint marks a point within a transaction

CallableStatement calls stored procedures
ResultSet holds data retrieved from a query

Performance tuning optimizes queries and indexes

Query optimizer chooses efficient execution plan
Logging records database operations for recovery
Monitoring tools track database health and performance
Authentication verifies user identity
Authorization determines user privileges
Encryption protects data by converting it to unreadable format
